line.comment: * Mayhem.Task.Worker.Looter
* Task 0.
* Expanded 2.2.1: worthwhile partial salvage and per-sector assignments.
* Based on the Renegades worker contract and Expanded gameplay requirements.
* Salvage Crew
* Initialize state used by subroutines (MSCI compiler requires earlier assignment).
* Sorting and planning arrays are rebuilt for each sector survey.
* Track cargo actually collected by this worker; equipment is not salvage.
* Recover from a prior task restart without leaving this ship's old reservation behind.
* Do not start another salvage assignment if docking failed.
* Use the Outpost's reach; player and AI Looters obey the same range.
* Do not dispatch another sector assignment at or above 60% occupied.
* Cargo capacity and thresholds were initialized once at startup.
* Choose the nearest remaining reachable sector from the ship's CURRENT position.
* One minimum scan instead of maintaining sorted copies of the sector array.
* Recheck this same target after an opportunistic homebase unload.
* It has already been removed from $sectorsLeft.
* The remote capacity survey does not require nearest-first sorting.
* Threat assessment is performed only for a sector worth salvaging.
* Opportunistic unload: if homebase lies on a shortest jump route to the chosen salvage sector,
* bank the cargo collected so far and resume evaluating THIS SAME candidate.
* Never detour with an empty salvage load.
* A sector with three enemies (or a hostile capital ship) is not a safe stop.
* Reuse the sector danger check without changing the selected destination.
* A new choice after this one must compute jumps from the new position.
* Reserve the whole sector BEFORE travelling to it.
* Recheck danger after arriving in the salvage sector.
* Enemy ships may have entered while the Looter was traveling.
* Survey on arrival, including assignments that started in the current sector.
* Stop if the Looter is no longer in its assigned sector.
* Bound movement/catch attempts, including continually respawning cargo.
* Partial assignments follow the precomputed value-aware collection plan.
* A fitting strategic or high-value crate cannot be crowded out by an unrelated smaller crate merely because the search returned it first.
* Read planned order from index zero; MSCI for each reads from the tail.
* If the plan is depleted (or all salvage fits), collect any other whole crate that still fits, using proximity to minimize movement.
* For each starts at the tail.
* The crate may have vanished or moved while we traveled.
* Do not pursue a repeatedly unreachable/uncollectible crate forever.
* Only actual successful collection warrants an en-route unload.
* Consume this planned attempt, whether successful or not.
* In whole-sector mode, finish all feasible crates even if crossing 60% full.
* In partial mode, fill with whole crates and then return home.
* Otherwise loop directly to the next nearby candidate.
* All candidates exhausted; unload before starting a new dispatch cycle.
* Unreachable candidates cannot be selected; terminate this dispatch cycle.
* One consistent filter shared by the survey and the actual collection loop.
* Inspect eligible whole crates, but do not pack them in find-array order.
* All observed eligible salvage can fit, and the 100-crate cap was not hit.
* Evaluate three different greedy packings, rather than relying on search order.
* First handle strategic cargo, highest market value first.
* Separate data arrays keep the sort keys aligned even if sort mutates data.
* Compare three candidate orders: highest value, largest size, smallest size.
* Build each order head-first, preserving priority before ordinary crates.
* A plan is a set of complete crates that can fit simultaneously.
* Simulate in the planned head-first order, not MSCI's tail-first for each order.
* Prefer a worthwhile plan with the greater credit value, using volume as a tiebreaker.
* All three plans reserve strategic materials first.
* A single Big Ship (which includes Huge Ship) makes the sector unsafe.
* Poll rather than use high-priority signal interrupts for movement safety.
* Compatibility with old task instances that only set destination/sector.
* Unload and maintain only after successful docking.
* The normal worker drop-off also clears the en-route salvage flag.
* Do so only when the ship is actually docked at its homebase.
